# Roundtrip Fixpoint Auditor

## Background

A document toolchain is only trustworthy when its serializers are *stable*: exporting a parsed document and importing the result back must eventually stop changing the artifact. This environment ships the Docling library preinstalled (v2.107.0 or newer, with all default model weights pre-baked) and is fully offline — no network access, no cloud APIs, no external services of any kind. A small corpus of hand-written source documents is already present in the project.

Build a format-stability auditor: it cycles every corpus document through two independent serialization channels, measures what changes on every cycle, finds the fixpoint, classifies the instabilities it finds and enforces a stability gate.

## Requirements

* A rerunnable command-line tool that audits every eligible document of a corpus directory through iterated export/import cycles in the `markdown` and `json` channels, plus one read-only HTML observation per document.
* Per-iteration measurements against the previous iteration: byte equality, normalized-text equality, structural equivalence of the parsed document model, and a similarity score.
* Fixpoint detection, per-run classification with stable codes, and a stability gate wired to process exit codes.
* Persistence of every intermediate serialization, a machine-readable report, per-document detail artifacts and a human-readable summary.
* Byte-level deterministic outputs.

## Implementation Hints

### Invocation

* Project path: `/home/user/fixpoint`
* Command: `python3 audit.py`
* Options (all optional, exact spelling):
  * `--corpus <dir>` (default `corpus`)
  * `--out <dir>` (default `out`)
  * `--max-iterations <int>` (default `3`, valid range 2..10 inclusive)
  * `--min-similarity <float>` (default `0.95`, valid range 0.0..1.0 inclusive)
  * `--doc <document_id>` — repeatable; when present, restricts the audit to exactly the listed document ids
* Relative path arguments resolve against the current working directory.

### Corpus and document ids

* Eligible source files are the regular files located directly inside the corpus directory (no recursion) whose lowercased extension is `.md` or `.html`. Every other entry is ignored.
* A document id is the source file name without its extension.
* The invocation is invalid (exit `2`, see "Gate and exit codes") when: the corpus path does not exist or is not a directory; no eligible file is found; two eligible files share the same document id; or a `--doc` value is not among the eligible document ids.

### Channels and the iterated cycle

* The channels are exactly `json` and `markdown`. The `json` channel uses Docling's lossless JSON serialization of the document model, the `markdown` channel uses Markdown. Their artifact extensions are `.json` and `.md`.
* `D0` is the document model parsed from the source file. For iteration `i` (1-based): `T_i` is the channel serialization of `D_(i-1)` as text, and `D_i` is the document model parsed back from `T_i`. Every run performs exactly `--max-iterations` (`K`) iterations, producing `T_1 .. T_K`, regardless of early convergence.
* Every `T_i` is written UTF-8 encoded to `<out>/documents/<document_id>/<channel>/iter_<NN>.<ext>`, where `NN` is the iteration number zero-padded to two digits.
* Independently of the cycles, `D0` is exported to HTML exactly once per document and written UTF-8 encoded to `<out>/documents/<document_id>/observation.html`. This is an observation only: it never takes part in a cycle, a classification or the gate.

### Normalized text

`normalize(s)` is defined as, in this exact order: (1) apply Unicode NFC; (2) replace every `CR LF` and then every remaining `CR` with `LF`; (3) replace every TAB (U+0009) and every NO-BREAK SPACE (U+00A0) with one SPACE (U+0020); (4) split into lines on `LF`; (5) in every line collapse each run of two or more SPACE characters into one SPACE, then strip leading and trailing SPACE characters; (6) drop the lines that are empty at this point; (7) join the surviving lines with a single `LF`.

### Similarity

`similarity(a, b)` operates on `normalize(a)` and `normalize(b)`: split both on whitespace into the token lists `A` and `B`; when both are empty the value is `1.0`; otherwise the value is `2 * S / (len(A) + len(B))` where `S` is the sum, over the distinct tokens `t`, of `min(count of t in A, count of t in B)`. Every similarity value that is stored or printed is rounded to 6 decimal places, half away from zero.

### Structure signature

The structure signature of a document model is an object with exactly these keys:

* `item_counts`: object mapping a label to the number of content items carrying it, counting every content item reachable from the document body. A key is the label the document model reports for the item, lowercased, with every character outside `[a-z0-9]` replaced by `_`. Labels with no occurrence are omitted.
* `max_depth`: integer; the greatest depth reached in the body tree, where the direct children of the body root have depth 1, and `0` when the body has no children.
* `table_dims`: array of `[rows, cols]` integer pairs, one per table of the document, in document order.

### Per-iteration record

For every iteration `i` record an object with exactly these keys: `iteration` (int, 1-based), `bytes` (int, the byte length of the UTF-8 encoded `T_i`), `sha256` (lowercase hex digest of the UTF-8 encoded `T_i`), `normalized_sha256` (lowercase hex digest of the UTF-8 encoded `normalize(T_i)`), `byte_equal_to_previous` (bool, `T_i` equals `T_(i-1)` byte for byte), `normalized_equal_to_previous` (bool, `normalize(T_i)` equals `normalize(T_(i-1))`), `similarity_to_previous` (number, `similarity(T_i, T_(i-1))`), `structure` (the structure signature of `D_i`) and `structure_equal_to_previous` (bool, the structure signature of `D_i` equals the one of `D_(i-1)`). Iteration 1 has no previous iteration: its three booleans are `false` and its `similarity_to_previous` is `0.0`.

### Fixpoint and classification

* `fixpoint_iteration` is the smallest `i` in `1..K-1` for which `T_i` equals `T_(i+1)` byte for byte, and `null` when there is none. `converged` is `true` exactly when `fixpoint_iteration` is not `null`.
* Every run gets exactly one code; the first matching rule wins, and "final record" means the record whose `iteration` equals `K`:
  1. `fixpoint_iteration` is `1` → `STABLE_IMMEDIATE`
  2. `fixpoint_iteration` is not `null` → `STABLE_DELAYED`
  3. the final record's `normalized_equal_to_previous` is `true` → `WHITESPACE_DRIFT`
  4. the final record's `structure_equal_to_previous` is `true` → `TEXT_DRIFT`
  5. otherwise → `STRUCTURE_DRIFT`
* The `final_similarity` of a run is the final record's `similarity_to_previous`.

### Gate and exit codes

Walk the runs in report order (document id ascending, then channel ascending) and append to `violations`: first `<document_id>/<channel>:<code>` when the code is neither `STABLE_IMMEDIATE` nor `STABLE_DELAYED`, then `<document_id>/<channel>:LOW_SIMILARITY` when `final_similarity` is lower than `--min-similarity`. The gate passes exactly when `violations` is empty.

* exit `0`: the audit completed and the gate passed.
* exit `3`: the audit completed and the gate failed; every artifact is still written in full.
* exit `2`: the invocation is invalid — the corpus/`--doc` cases listed above, or `--max-iterations` / `--min-similarity` outside their valid range or not parseable as the required type. Then nothing at all is printed on stdout, stderr carries at least one line that starts with `error: ` (this also applies to argument-parsing failures, so the default parser diagnostics are not sufficient on their own), and the output directory and its contents are neither created, deleted nor modified.

### Output artifacts

On a valid invocation the tool first removes all existing contents of the output directory (creating that directory when it is missing), then writes:

* `<out>/report.json`
* `<out>/summary.txt`
* `<out>/documents/<document_id>/detail.json`
* `<out>/documents/<document_id>/observation.html`
* `<out>/documents/<document_id>/<channel>/iter_<NN>.<ext>`

`report.json` and every `detail.json` are UTF-8 encoded, indented with 2 spaces, have their object keys sorted ascending at every nesting level, leave non-ASCII characters unescaped (a document id carrying non-ASCII characters therefore appears verbatim), and end with exactly one newline character. The iteration artifacts of the `json` channel are not constrained beyond being the channel's own serialization.

`report.json` is an object with exactly these keys:

* `schema_version`: the string `1.0`
* `corpus`: the absolute, resolved path of the corpus directory
* `max_iterations`: int
* `min_similarity`: number
* `channels`: the array `["json", "markdown"]`
* `documents`: array ordered by `document_id` ascending; every entry has exactly `document_id` (string), `source_file` (the source file name including its extension), `html_sha256` (lowercase hex digest of the observation HTML bytes) and `runs`
* every entry of `runs` has exactly `channel`, `iterations` (int, equal to `max_iterations`), `fixpoint_iteration` (int or `null`), `converged` (bool), `code` (string) and `final_similarity` (number), ordered by `channel` ascending
* `totals`: exactly `documents` (int), `runs` (int), `converged_runs` (int), `codes` (object carrying all five codes as keys and their run counts as values) and `min_final_similarity` (number, the smallest `final_similarity` over all runs)
* `gate`: exactly `passed` (bool), `exit_code` (int, the process exit code) and `violations` (array of strings)

`<out>/documents/<document_id>/detail.json` is an object with exactly the keys `document_id`, `source_file`, `source_sha256` (lowercase hex digest of the source file bytes), `html_sha256`, `html_bytes` (int, byte length of the observation HTML) and `channels`. `channels` is an object keyed by channel name whose values have exactly the keys `code`, `converged`, `fixpoint_iteration`, `final_similarity`, `artifacts` (array of the iteration artifact paths relative to the document directory, in iteration order) and `iterations` (array of the per-iteration records, in iteration order).

### summary.txt and stdout

`summary.txt` is UTF-8 encoded with LF line endings and has exactly `9 + R` lines, `R` being the number of runs:

* line 1: `FIXPOINT AUDIT`
* line 2: `corpus: <absolute corpus path>`
* line 3: `documents: <number of audited documents>`
* line 4: `runs: <number of runs>`
* line 5: `max_iterations: <int>`
* line 6: `min_similarity: <value with exactly 6 decimals>`
* line 7: empty
* lines 8 .. 7+R: one line per run in report order, formatted as `<document_id> <channel> <code> fixpoint=<n> similarity=<value>` with single spaces between the five fields, `<n>` being the fixpoint iteration or `-` when there is none, and `<value>` the final similarity with exactly 6 decimals
* line 8+R: empty
* line 9+R: `GATE: PASS` when the gate passed, otherwise `GATE: FAIL (<v> violations)` with `<v>` the number of violations

The file ends with exactly one newline character. On exit `0` and exit `3` stdout must be byte-identical to the contents of `summary.txt`; any diagnostics belong on stderr.

### Determinism

Re-running the tool with the same corpus and the same options must produce byte-identical `report.json`, `summary.txt`, `detail.json` and iteration artifacts. Do not embed timestamps, durations, random values, or host-specific paths other than the ones specified above.

import importlib.metadata

def _resolve_version() -> str:
